name: Stratum Chrome-Vent Augment Specialist Set
description:
A Tier 4 specialist suit designed explicitly for heavily augmented workers who have grown tired of pretending their chrome doesn't exist. The jacket is a structured single-breasted cut in Stratum's 'Ironweave Coolform' — a matte dark slate fabric with a subtle crosshatch texture — tailored with open chrome-channel sleeves: both sleeves terminate at mid-forearm in a clean folded cuff with a wide magnetic-closure opening, designed so that chrome arms or prosthetic forearms can extend naturally without the fabric bunching or tearing. The channels are finished in exposed brushed steel binding that runs along the interior seam from shoulder to cuff, visible at the opening — a deliberate design choice that treats the augmentation as part of the silhouette rather than something to be hidden. The back panel has a reinforced spinal-rig dorsal channel: a structured spine of the jacket that accommodates external rig hardware, with three adjustment points that can be loosened via a side-access pull. The dress shirt beneath is a Stratum Executive Poplin in pale graphite with a standard cutaway collar, its sleeves cut short intentionally to sit at the bicep — the chrome-channel jacket cuff is meant to do the work from there.

Trousers are straight-cut Stratum Ironweave Coolform with a high rise and no break, worn with a slim brushed-steel-buckle belt. Footwear is the Crucible Chromestep Mid in matte black with steel cap, chosen for its visual echo of the chrome hardware at the wrists. The whole outfit leans into augmentation as aesthetic rather than hiding it — the chrome bindings, the open-channel cuffs, the spinal rig channel. This is someone who has stopped apologizing for their hardware and started treating it as a credential.
functionality: Open chrome-channel sleeves with magnetic closures for bilateral arm augmentation. Spinal rig dorsal channel with three external adjustment points. Coolform fabric actively dissipates heat from aug hardware. Short-cut poplin sleeves designed to pair with channel jacket. High-rise trouser waistband compatible with lower-back rig harness straps. Steel-cap footwear for work-floor safety compliance on specialist site visits.
what_it_says: This person is augmented, skilled, and done with the corporate aesthetic of pretending otherwise. The chrome bindings say: I am modified, I am competent, and I chose an outfit that accommodates both rather than apologizing for either. It sits at the exact edge of acceptable Tier 4 rule-bending — bold enough to be noticed, structured enough to be defensible.
worn_by: corporate engineering leads with bilateral chrome arms
senior fabrication supervisors on client presentation days
story_hooks: A Tier 3 HR officer tells the wearer the exposed chrome binding on the cuffs violates the dress code for a cross-tier meeting — the wearer produces the Stratum product documentation proving the outfit is rated 'presentation-compliant,' and the argument that follows reveals more about the company's attitude toward augmented workers than either party intended.

The spinal rig dorsal channel's adjustment points snag on a security scanner turnstile, locking the wearer briefly in place during a timed evacuation drill — not dangerous, but humiliating in front of Tier 5 observers.

Another heavily augmented specialist in an identical outfit shows up to the same client meeting — both are from different competing firms, and the accidental twinning becomes a strange icebreaker that shifts the negotiation's dynamics entirely.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sharply tailored Tier 4 specialist ensemble that celebrates augmentation rather than concealing it. The structured jacket presents a clean, corporate silhouette with deliberate architectural breaks at the forearms and spine—intentional voids that frame chrome hardware as design elements. The wearer reads as confident, augment-forward, and proudly non-baseline. Posture-forward and assertive.
physical_description.fit: Tailored but not restrictive. Single-breasted jacket with structured shoulders sits close to the frame without binding. High-rise trousers with a straight leg and no break create a vertical emphasis. The chrome-channel sleeves are cut to sit flush at mid-forearm, allowing augmented limbs to extend naturally. Overall impression: professional, purposeful, unapologetic.
physical_description.primary_material: Stratum Ironweave Coolform (matte dark slate synth-blend with thermal regulation properties). Pale graphite Executive Poplin for the dress shirt. Brushed steel binding and hardware throughout. Matte black leather/synthleather hybrid for footwear with reinforced steel toe cap.
physical_description.texture: Crosshatch weave visible on the jacket fabric—subtle, industrial, catches light differently depending on angle. The exposed brushed steel bindings have a warm matte finish with visible grain. Shirt poplin is smooth and crisp. Chrome-channel openings reveal the textured interior seam detail.
physical_description.color_scheme: Dominant: matte dark slate (almost charcoal). Secondary: pale graphite. Accents: brushed steel (warm metallic gray). All colors desaturated and cool-toned, creating a unified chromatic palette that treats metal hardware as a neutral rather than a contrast.
physical_description.closures: Jacket: standard button front (brushed steel buttons embedded in the Ironweave). Chrome-channel cuffs: wide magnetic snap closures (invisible until engaged). Trousers: hidden magnetic waistband closure (typical Stratum Corp standard). Belt: brushed steel buckle with friction-fit closure. Shoes: pressure-lace system with steel eyelets.
distinctive_features: Open chrome-channel sleeves with folded cuff design and exposed brushed steel binding
Reinforced spinal-rig dorsal channel on back panel with three side-access adjustment points
Deliberately short dress shirt sleeves (cut to bicep) to expose the transition to augmented forearm
Visible interior seam detailing in the chrome channels—treats hardware as part of the aesthetic
High-rise, no-break trouser cut emphasizes vertical line and augmented lower limbs
Crucible Chromestep Mid footwear in matte black with steel cap—visual echo of wrist hardware
Brushed steel belt buckle and buttons create a coordinated hardware language
Stratum corporate branding subtly embossed on the jacket interior collar
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 4—Working class with corporate sponsorship and augmentation investment. Not wealthy enough for bespoke corpo luxury (Tier 1-2), but too augmented and specialized for basic Tier 5 street wear. The Stratum line is explicitly designed for augment-forward workers who have legitimacy through corporation affiliation.
physical_description.cultural_context: Wearer signals: augmentation specialist, corporate-aligned field technician, someone past the point of corpo pretense about their chrome. This is the uniform of augment riggers, rig-maintenance specialists, heavy-load handlers, and corp-side medical techs. Wearing this says 'my augmentation is functional, credential-bearing, and I'm not hiding it.' Not military (too tailored), not corpo executive (too honest about the chrome), not street (too structured). Pure specialist worker.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine to broken-in. Stratum Ironweave is treated to resist wear, so new suits look almost aggressively new. After a few months of use, the crosshatch weave begins to show depth, the brushed steel develops a subtle patina, and the magnetic closures acquire faint fingerprint marks. Well-maintained specimens show zero fraying or damage—durability is a selling point. Worn examples may have scuff marks on the steel toe cap or slight stress marks around the adjustment points on the dorsal channel, but never look shabby.
